analysis.title: ISM Manufacturing Index Rebounded in October, In Expansion Throughout 2026
key_insights: The ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5 in September, the second-highest reading of 2026 and just below July's 55.6. A reading above 50 indicates expansion.
The index has been in expansion every month in 2026, after being below 50 almost all of the time from late 2022 to the end of 2025.
Four of the five subcomponents rose in October and all five were above 50. Production rose to 59.0 from 56.7, the highest since late 2021.
Inventories moved into expansion at 51.4 from 48.6. New orders and supplier deliveries also rose. Employment fell to 52.4 from 52.7 but stayed in expansion for a fourth straight month.

Among the subindices outside the headline calculation, imports and new export orders rose, order backlog and prices paid fell, and customer inventories were flat. Customer inventories were the only one below 50.

Twelve of eighteen industries reported expansion. The strongest were plastics and rubber, electrical equipment, machinery, and computer and electronic products. Three reported contraction: printing, paper products, and non-metallic mineral products.
Much of the growth comes from very strong tech investment, with signs it is broadening to other manufacturing industries.
Respondent comments were generally negative despite the solid headline. They cited strong AI-related demand, but also high fuel and input prices and elevated uncertainty.

Manufacturing employment is up 72,000 so far in 2026 but still down 250,000 from early 2023. Industrial production has risen gradually since late 2024 but remains slightly below its late-2021 and pre-pandemic levels.
PNC expects manufacturing to keep expanding through the rest of 2026 and into 2027, citing AI-related investment, improving non-AI capital spending and solid consumer demand.
